Anna L: Heads-up — I ran a short bake of the prefix/KV cold-starts using the new prefetch heuristics. Seeing a weird high p99 tail when concurrent clients hit cold partitions. Putting notes + repro plan here so we don't lose it.

Anna L: TL;DR: under synthetic replay with 4x concurrency we see p50 ~30ms, p95 ~120ms, but p99 jumps to 420ms. Single-client replay doesn't show the tail. Suspect eviction+kernel-switch interaction + batching warmup.

Raj P: Thanks. Can you paste the exact load config and command you used?

Anna L: Sure — command: `./replay_driver --trace traces/prefix_hotspot.json --concurrency 4 --rps 400 --seed 2026 --warmup 60 --duration 300 --kv-mode prefetch`

Anna L: Load config excerpt:
```json
{
  "concurrency": 4,
  "rps": 400,
  "sequence_len": {"p50": 40, "p95": 128},
  "kv_prefetch_enabled": true,
  "batching": {"max_tokens": 2048, "max_batch_size": 32},
  "kv_cache_size": 200000
}
```

Emily K: Good. Did you isolate kernel selection changes? We landed the mini-kernel switch two weeks ago. Could be a regression where small batches pick a slower kernel under contention.

Anna L: I ran a kernel-blacklist run (force old kernel) and tail disappears. So kernel selection is definitely involved. But only when KV misses spike during warmup.

Dmitri: Can you share perf profile? flamegraph/symbols?

Anna L: Pasted the perf output (reduced):
```
  38.2%  runtime  [.] kv_cache::populate_prefix
  21.7%  runtime  [.] kernels::dispatch::select_kernel
   9.8%  runtime  [.] batching::batch_assembly
   6.5%  runtime  [.] memory::alloc
   4.0%  libc     [.] memcpy
```

Anna L: The flamegraph shows big spikes in `select_kernel` when several requests arrive and batches are formed while KV lookups are pending. Kernel selection runs a few heuristics that inspect kv hitrate & sequence length distribution — which in cold-start can flip flops.

Raj P: Sounds like heuristic oscillation. Two ideas: 1) make selection sticky for N seconds after first choose, 2) incorporate inflight-kv fraction into decision so preferring kernels optimized for smaller effective batch when inflight KV > X.

Emily K: Agree. Also check KV eviction churn — if prefetch populates many entries but evictions happen concurrently, hitrate metrics seen by the selector might be lying. What's eviction rate?

Anna L: From logs in that run: `evictions/sec =~ 180` during warmup phase, then drops to ~10. That's pretty high. We might be thrashing the cache initially because prefetch bursts push many prefixes in.

Dmitri: Could be capacity config mismatch vs replay trace. How do the traces scale key space vs baseline?

Anna L: This trace is a synthetic hotspot: 70% of requests hit 3000 top prefixes, rest are long-tail. We set cache size to 200k so should be fine, but prefetch bursts push many internal representations (large memory per entry). So it's memory pressure + eviction.

perf-bot: Deploy note: e2e-replay-2026-03-17 failed with p99>400ms (eng-runtime). Linked run: https://ci.redwood/replays/1899876543

Raj P: Repro plan suggestion: 1) Replay with `--kv-mode no-prefetch` to confirm prefetch involvement; 2) Replay with `--kernel-force=old` and `--kernel-force=new` to compare; 3) Run with `--concurrency 1,2,4,8` to find concurrency threshold; 4) Instrument eviction counters into selector logging.

Anna L: I already did 1 & 2. No-prefetch removes tail. Force-old removes tail. So it's an intersection: prefetch causes KV churn which triggers selector to pick different kernel resulting in bad batch formation.

Emily K: Can you capture a narrow window with `--trace-sampling=1s --extra-metrics=selector_state,kvcache_stats,batch_sizes` for the problematic interval? We need a per-second view to see oscillation.

Anna L: Will run and attach. Also planning to diff memory footprints with `JE_MALLOC_CONF` to rule out allocator-induced latency.

Dmitri: For apples-to-apples: ensure both kernels run with identical `max_batch_size` and `streaming` flags. Kernel implementations have minor defaults that can bias latency.

Anna L: Good call. My previous force-old run didn't override `streaming` flag — will re-run with explicit flags.

Raj P: Longer-term fix idea: make selector cost-model aware of outstanding KV latency distribution. If outstanding KV lookups are high, bias towards kernels that prioritize lower head-latency (smaller batching) to avoid long p99 tails.

Emily K: And add a short hysteresis window to avoid flipping on transient drops. 1-2s glue probably enough.

Anna L: Repro results (first follow-up run):
- `--kv-mode no-prefetch` concurrency=4 p99=95ms
- `--kv-mode prefetch` concurrency=4 p99=420ms
- `--kernel-force=old --kv-mode prefetch` concurrency=4 p99=110ms
- `--kernel-force=new --kv-mode prefetch` concurrency=4 p99=430ms

Anna L: So new kernel + prefetch is the bad combo. But the selector chooses new kernel when it thinks batches will be large; during warmup with inflight KV this guess is wrong and we get slow path.

Dmitri: Next diagnostic: log the `selector_decision` payload on every dispatch including `estimated_batch`, `inflight_kv_fraction`, `kv_eviction_rate`, `chosen_kernel`, `lookup_latency_ms`. Add sampling to avoid log spam.

Anna L: Added that to a local build. Example log line: `selector=pick kernel=new estimated_batch=24 inflight_kv=0.72 evict_s=180 lookup_p50=35ms chosen=new`

Raj P: For tests: add a deterministic replay that injects a fixed KV lookup delay (e.g., 50ms) to simulate cold backend without prefetch. Then you can tune selector to react to inflight fraction rather than raw hitrate.

Emily K: Also try reducing prefetch aggressiveness: limit prefetch concurrency `--prefetch-parallel=4` and add exponential backoff per key when eviction rate exceeds threshold.

Anna L: I'll run 3 more variants today and open a bench PR with configs and graphs. Planning to include: load driver command, trace metadata, perf flamegraphs, selector logs, and memory snapshots.

perf-bot: Reminder: attach run ids and sizes for compliance.

Dmitri: Once we have deterministic repro, we should add an integration test in `eng-runtime/replay-tests` that fails on p99 regression > 2x baseline. Make it run nightly on the perf cluster.

Anna L: Agreed. I'll include a `repro/` directory with minimal trace + script to reproduce: `./reproduce.sh --seed 2026 --concurrency 4`. Will link the PR here.

Raj P: Excellent. Thanks Anna. If you want a quick patch, I'd try making the selector sticky-first-choice for 2s and cap `estimated_batch` by `(1 - inflight_kv_fraction) * max_batch_size` and see immediate effect.

Anna L: Will try that as an experiment. Posting results in ~2h. :coffee:

Emily K: Ping us if you want help with perf infra for capturing flamegraphs automatically.

Anna L: Thanks all — uploading the detailed run artifact now: https://artifacts.redwood/prefetch-repro-1899876543.tar.gz

perf-bot: Artifact uploaded: prefetch-repro-1899876543.tar.gz (size: 48MB)

Anna L: Update 2h later: sticky-selector=2s + capped estimate reduced p99 to 120ms in prefetch+new kernel run. Looks promising. Opening draft PR with config and benchmark notes.

Raj P: Nice! Follow-up: we should add a unit test for the selector that simulates inflight_kv scenarios.

Anna L: Will add tests. Closing loop once PR lands.

Emily K: Great work.

Dmitri: :thumbsup:
